title: Zanzibar Mahamri
community: Zanzibar — the purest expression of the mahamri tradition
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Zanzibar Mahamri — the island's definitive version of the Swahili coconut doughnut. Made with pure thick Zanzibar coconut milk, double cardamom, and a resting period that produces a lighter, more fragrant result than mainland mahamri. Eaten with mbaazi wa Nazi every morning in Zanzibar.
longDesc: Zanzibar mahamri are distinguished from mainland mahamri by the higher ratio of coconut milk (no water), the more generous cardamom, and the longer rest period. Made from Zanzibar's own fresh coconut milk, they are richer, more fragrant, and more golden than any other version.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, cardamom, and salt.
Beat egg into warm coconut milk. Add rose water if using.
Pour into dry ingredients. Mix to a soft, slightly tacky dough — add more coconut milk if needed.
Roll to 1cm thickness. Cut into triangles.
Fry at 170°C for 3—4 minutes per batch, turning, until deeply golden.
chefTips: Pure coconut milk — no water — is what makes Zanzibar mahamri.
Double cardamom compared to mainland mahamri.
Longer rest produces a lighter result.
cookingScience: See TZA006 for mahamri cooking science.
culturalNote: Zanzibar mahamri are the gold standard of this Swahili doughnut — richer, more fragrant, and more golden than any version made elsewhere. They are the mahamri that all other mahamri aspire to be.
